name: EAQuant: Enhancing Post-Training Quantization for MoE Models via Expert-Aware Optimization
problem: Dense PTQ methods ignore that MoE routing is a DISCRETE decision: small quantization perturbations can change which experts are selected and thereby change the computation path.
mechanism: Three expert-aware components, each aimed at a named failure mode: (1) smoothing aggregation to suppress activation outliers using the MoE aggregation weights; (2) ROUTING CONSISTENCY ALIGNMENT - a penalty term that pushes the post-quantization top-k expert selection toward matching the pre-quantization selection, so the computation path is preserved; (3) calibration data balance so sparsely-activated experts still get calibrated. The routing-consistency term is the distinguishing idea and is shared in spirit with VSRAQ.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): across W4A4 / W3A4 / W3A3 / W2A4 settings on three MoE architectures, average accuracy improvements of 1.15-13.81% over existing methods, with largest gains on reasoning tasks. COMPRESSION RATIO: down to 2-bit weights with 4-bit activations (W2A4) is the most aggressive setting reported, i.e. up to ~8x on weights. QUALITY COST: 1.15-13.81% average accuracy gain over baselines - a wide band that shows how much the baselines vary by architecture.
